Commander. Joint Base Lewis-McChord. HIGH OPSEC exposure identified across two vectors.

HIGH — Aircraft. 25 military flights logged on public ADS-B trackers in the last 7 days. Callsigns RAGE80 and STING54 show a recurring pattern on Tuesday, Friday, and Sunday between 0600 and 1000. Predictable flight windows create targetable vulnerabilities.

HIGH — Satellite imaging. Sentinel-2A pass in approximately 6 minutes at 10 degrees elevation. 19 passes within the next 24 hours. High frequency of imaging opportunities increases risk of outdoor activities being captured.

MINIMAL — Fitness activity. No Strava heatmap data available. No predictable personnel movement patterns exposed.

Composite exposure score: 42 out of 100. Risk level: MEDIUM.

Recommended actions. One: file FAA LADD blocking for callsigns RAGE80 and STING54 immediately. Two: adjust flight schedules to reduce predictability, especially during 0600 to 1000 windows. Three: reschedule outdoor activities to avoid satellite pass times. Four: maintain current OPSEC protocols for fitness tracking to ensure continued minimal exposure.

[Note: ADS-B traffic is synthetic for V1 — derived from the populated Units/Platforms ontology. To be replaced by Member A's real ADS-B Exchange capture when available.]
